reasons.plausibility: The hypothesis is scientifically sound: Ta has lower electronegativity than Mo, similar atomic size, and is a known BCC stabilizer, so partial substitution should reduce bonding heterogeneity and improve plasticity while largely retaining solid-solution strength, though the exact 20% threshold and quantitative strength retention are uncertain.
reasons.testability: The proposed test is clear and feasible, with specific alloy preparation, structural characterization, and quantitative falsification criteria (strength drop >10%, plasticity increase <20%), though the 20% plasticity improvement threshold may be arbitrary.
reasons.usefulness: The hypothesis directly addresses the research question with a concrete, actionable intervention and a well-defined mechanism, making it highly relevant and worth testing for researchers working on this alloy system.
